regenerable_on: a guest running BOTH clients — transmission's RPC and sabnzbd's JSON API, with SE_TRANSMISSION_URL, SE_SABNZBD_URL and SE_SABNZBD_API_KEY handed to se-capture-guest — and carrying transfers in both. The replay seam pins all three configuration gates, so a one-client guest cannot re-stage this variant at all: it would replay as a client that could not be asked. The transfers are STAGED, not found: three torrents built from metainfo minted at capture time (announcing to tracker.invalid, so the swarm is empty by construction) and two sabnzbd jobs built from NZBs whose segments name message-ids that exist nowhere. Every figure below is this pair of daemons' own state at that moment, so a re-stage moves all of them and the anchors are re-read by hand in the same change, or they are asserting a machine that is gone.
anonymisation_note: Scrubbed against harness/scrub/downloaders.json, three substitutions: transmission's session-id (its CSRF nonce, format serial) and both sabnzbd nzo ids (UUIDs, so the free-text pass rewrote them into the 5cb0… convention). Everything else is verbatim, and harness/scrub/downloaders.json states the bounds under which each verbatim classification holds — the torrent names, the info-hashes and the in-container paths are all `nothing` because of what this guest happens to run, and every one of those entries says so and says what a real host's capture must do instead. The independent detectors (harness/se_harness/detectors.py) were run over the committed bytes afterwards and found nothing.
note:
Two clients, two collections, and the row counts deliberately disagree with the counts the clients report about themselves.

What this variant exists to teach is that `clients` and `transfers` are answers from two different vantages. sabnzbd holds two queue slots and states QueueCount 1, because `noofslots_total` counts the slots that are not paused and the second job is — so a port that derived QueueCount from the length of the slots list agrees with the reference about the transfers and disagrees about the client, on the same document. Transmission's three counts are three different numbers for the same reason: 2 active, 1 paused, 3 held. They were two and two until a third torrent was staged for this capture, and equal numbers would have let a port that read the wrong counter pass.

The absences are half of what a downloader row says. Transmission answered `download-dir-free-space: -1` — the container's download directory is not where the daemon can measure it — so DiskFreeBytes is OMITTED rather than published as -1 or as 0, and DiskTotalBytes is absent because transmission states free space with no denominator at all (rule 7: no percentage without a denominator the source stated). The reverse holds on the other row: sabnzbd states both, in GB, and the adapter converts once. Every sabnzbd transfer lacks Error, ErrorString, IsStalled and the three byte-valued facts, and every transmission transfer lacks SizeMB, LeftMB and TimeLeft, because those are the two clients' own vocabularies and neither is translated into the other's.

Stated bounds, because a specimen shows one machine on one day.

No transfer here is in trouble. Every torrent reports error 0 with an empty errorString and isStalled false, and neither sabnzbd slot reports a fault, so ErrorString is published by nothing in this pair and the `if error != 0 and errorString` arm of torrent_facts is reached by no row. That is the shape the differential guard's `transmission-errored-transfer` operator mints, and conformance/fixtures/adversaries/a9_transfer_error_blind.py is the port it exists to catch — a capture cannot draw a distinction none of its rows exhibits.

Of transmission's seven documented states this capture holds two: `download` (4) and `stopped` (0). check-wait, check, download-wait, seed-wait and seed are unreached, and `seed` is the one a completed torrent sits in indefinitely — a port whose status table stopped at the values it had met would be right about every row here.

No failure path is exercised. A client configured but unreachable (StatusUnobservable), a sabnzbd URL with no key (ConfigMissing), and a host with no client configured at all are three different statements this collector makes and no committed capture stages any of them. The last one is the interesting absence: with neither URL set the shipping adapter returns an empty list for both collections and the reference commits zero objects with NO decline record, which is authoritative-empty — the Go port declines `absent` and commits zero instead, and the live comparator is where that disagreement gets adjudicated.

And the rows carry values only: no names family, no absent list, no unobservable record, no relation assertion. The `tracks` and `dispatches-to` edges this subsystem is the other end of are emitted by the servarr adapter, not by this one.
anchors_note:
Read off payloads/ by hand at staging, before any stream existed, which is what makes them an authority the reference-generated half is not. Every anchor below was checked twice for discrimination, and both passes were RUN. The payload member each anchor rests on was rewritten and the reference re-run over it, which is the pass that proves an anchor tracks the capture rather than the generated stream; and the committed stream was edited so that one anchor's claim was false, which is the pass that proves it would catch a port. Twenty-seven anchors discriminate under both. Five discriminate only under the second, because no payload member drives them: transmission's DiskTotalBytes and QueueCount, sabnzbd's TorrentCount, and a sabnzbd slot's SizeWhenDoneBytes and IsStalled are facts the adapter has NO code path to emit for that client, so nothing in a document can make them appear. What they assert is that a port must not invent them, and editing the stream is the only way to state that.

The objects are named by their NATIVE names, which is what the collector publishes: a torrent by its info-hash, lowercased, and a sabnzbd job by its nzo id. The ids the adapter mints — `client:transmission`, `transfer:sabnzbd/<nzo>` — are the collator's to derive from the declared prefix and these names, so an anchor on an id would be asserting the collator's work rather than the collector's. The two nzo ids are the SCRUBBED spelling, because that is what the committed payload carries; the three info-hashes are the real ones, because harness/scrub/downloaders.json classifies them `nothing` and says at length why that is a bound of this capture rather than a property of the field.

Transmission's three counts are anchored separately and all three differ — 3 held, 2 active, 1 paused. They were 2/1/1 when this capture was first taken, and a third torrent was staged precisely because two equal numbers would certify a port that read the wrong counter. The same discipline picks the transfer sizes: 1048576, 2097152 and 4194304 are three different figures, so an anchor cannot pass by matching whichever row was read first.

QueueCount 1 is the densest anchor here and it is deliberately NOT the number of transfer rows. sabnzbd holds two slots and reports `noofslots_total: 1`, because the paused job is not counted; the glossary says QueueCount is the client's own counting, and this is it. A port that answered `len(slots)` produces 2, passes every transfers anchor, and fails here — which is the whole reason the two collections are captured together.

DiskFreeBytes 9459665469 and DiskTotalBytes 15429670010 are the GB→byte conversion done once: sabnzbd states "8.81" and "14.37" as STRINGS of gigabytes, and 8.81 × 1024³ = 9459665469 (truncated, not rounded). A port that published the string, the float, or a 1000³ conversion fails all three ways, and none of them is visible to an untyped comparison.

PercentDone 0.0 is a float and Error 0 and IsStalled false are a present-and-zero int and a present-and-false boolean. Each catches a different reflex: a port that renders 0.0 as 0 fails typed equality, and a port that treated a falsy reading as an absence drops Error and IsStalled entirely. Both are readings, not omissions.

The seven absences are the half a value anchor cannot state, and each names a different reason. Transmission has no DiskFreeBytes because it answered -1, which is its own way of saying it cannot measure the directory — so the anchor discriminates between omission and the two wrong spellings a port reaches for, -1 and 0. It has no DiskTotalBytes and no QueueCount because it states neither, ever. sabnzbd has no TorrentCount for the same kind of reason from the other side. The transmission transfer has no ErrorString because its error code is 0; the sabnzbd transfer has no SizeWhenDoneBytes and no IsStalled because sabnzbd counts in megabytes and has no stall verdict. A port that translated one client's vocabulary into the other's fails these and passes every value anchor above.

commit_objects 2 and 5 are anchored because absence is not the only way to lose a collection: a port that published one row per client document, or that dropped the paused sabnzbd slot for looking inactive, satisfies every fact anchor above and reports a different number here. 5 is 3 torrents + 2 slots, from two documents.

Deliberately not anchored: transmission's session-id and every setting in session-get that no fact is lifted from, sabnzbd's `avg_age`, `time_added` and the `_norm` disk strings, and the cumulative/current stats blocks. No fact reads them, and anchoring one would pin this pair to a wall-clock moment a re-stage cannot reproduce. Also not anchored: RateDownloadBytes and RateUploadBytes on any row. They are 0 everywhere because nothing is moving, and an anchor on a zero that every member of a family shares certifies a port that read any of them.
